ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a completed RydeTAXI metered ride (F6), so over-distance enters the fare through the meter and the case is decided under RD-1/RD-2/RD-4 rather than FARE-1 [F6][RD-2]. Exactly one off-route segment exists: 17:38–17:49, 6.56 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, +4.92 km, up to 1911 m off the optimal line [F3][RD-1]. No rider message in the complete, timestamped chat agrees to any route change — the only messages are the 17:23 pickup note and the 17:24 driver reply — so RD-5 gives the driver nothing [F7][F8][F9][RD-5].

The driver instead claims reasonable cause under RD-4: an LTA DataMall accident on the Seletar Expressway (towards TPE) after the Woodlands Avenue 12 Exit, reported 17:16, 0 m from the optimal route, advising "avoid lane 2" [F13][F10][RD-4]. RD-4(a) requires the incident fact to sit on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, be reported before the segment began and still be listed within the trip window: 17:16 < 17:38 start, and the 17:28–18:01 window contains it, 0 m from the optimal corridor [F3][F13][RD-4]. That element the trace marks satisfied (✓ RD-4(a), incident within 300 m of optimal km 7.1–8.7), and it is settled by the record, not by the driver's post-trip narrative [F10][RD-4].

The speed-band facts do not assist either side: band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Seletar Expressway and band 4 on Tampines Expressway sit outside band 1–2, and RD-4(b) says a band alone cannot exempt a segment — they are corroboration only [F11][F12][RD-4]. The rider's point that the +30% distance and +10.2 min overrun (F1, F2) exceed what one lane-block explains is real, but RD-1 sets no percentage or kilometre threshold, and RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of segments that no clause excuses [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2]. Since RD-4(a) excuses the only segment, the refundable mileage is zero: 0 km × $1.4099/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The residual 0.18 km (5.10 km billed vs 4.92 km segmented) is unattributed loop/jitter and is not refundable in any event [F1][F4][RD-2].

RD-6 is not engaged: the trace marks the 90-day prior upheld route dispute count as 0, so even a finding on this segment would not make the breach "repeated" and no account flag attaches [F16][RD-6]. The rider's clean profile and the driver's rating change nothing — profile facts never decide a case [F15][F16][RD-6].
